edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ φάσκομεν αὐτὸν συγκεχύσθαι ἔκ τινων παρακουσμάτων, φέρε καὶ ταῦτα ἡμεῖς κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἡμῖν τρανώσωμεν καὶ παραστήσωμεν ὅτι, Κέλσου νομίζοντος Ἰουδαϊκὸν εἶναι τὸ προσκυνεῖν οὐρανῷ καὶ τοῖς ἐν αὐτῷ ἀγγέλοις, οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκὸν μὲν τὸ τοιοῦτον, παραβατικὸν δὲ ἰουδαϊσμοῦ ἐστιν, ὥσπερ καὶ τὸ προσκυνεῖν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς ἀγάλμασιν. εὑρήσεις γοῦν μάλιστα ἐν τῷ Ἱερεμίᾳ τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ λόγον, διὰ τοῦ προφήτου μεμφόμενον τῷ Ἰουδαίων λαῷ ὡς προσκυνοῦντι τὰ τοιαῦτα καὶ θύοντι „τῇ βασιλίσσῃ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ“ καὶ „πάσῃ τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.“ δηλοῦσι δὲ καὶ οἱ Χριστιανῶν λόγοι, κατηγοροῦντες τῶν ἐν Ἰουδαίοις ἁμαρτανομένων, ὅτι θεοῦ ἐγκαταλιπόντος τὸν λαὸν ἐκεῖνον ἐπί τισιν ἁμαρτήμασι καὶ ταῦτ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἡμαρτάνετο. ἐν μὲν γὰρ ταῖς Πράξεσι γέγραπται τῶν ἀποστόλων περὶ Ἰουδαίων ὅτι „ἔστρεψε δὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς λατρεύειν τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῶν προφητῶν· μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τεσσαράκοντα ἔτη, οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ ῾Ρομφᾶ. τοὺς τύπους, οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν αὐτοῖς;“ παρὰ δὲ τῷ Παύλῳ, ἀκριβῶς τὰ Ἰουδαίων παιδευθέντι καὶ ὕστερον ἐκ παραδόξου ἐπιφανείας Ἰησοῦ χριστιανίσαντι. τοιαῦτ᾿ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Κολασσαεῖς λέλεκται· „μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς καταβραβευέτω θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἃ ἑώρακεν ἐμβατεύων, εἰκῇ φυσιούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ νοὸς τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐ κρατῶν τὴν κεφαλὴν, ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν καὶ συνδέσμων ἐπιχορηγούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ θεοῦ.“ ταῦτα δὲ μήτ᾿ ἀναγνοὺς μήτε μαθὼν ὁ Κέλσος οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως πεποίηκεν ὡς οὐ παρανομοῦντας Ἰουδαίους προσκυνεῖν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ τοῖς ἐν αὐτῷ ἀγγέλοις.
thought_title: Worshipping heaven and angels breaks the Jewish law
pass_a_gloss: Since we assert that he was confused from some things misheard, come, let us also make these clear as far as possible for us and present/prove that, Celsus thinking it Jewish to worship heaven and the angels in it, such a thing is not Jewish but transgressive of Judaism, just as also worshipping sun and moon and stars but also statues/images. You will find at any rate especially in Jeremiah the word of God through the prophet blaming the people of the Jews as worshipping such things and sacrificing 'to the queen of heaven' and 'to all the host of heaven'. And the writings of Christians also show, accusing the things sinned among Jews, that, God having forsaken that people for certain sins, these also were sinned by them. For in the Acts of the apostles it is written concerning Jews that 'God turned and gave them over to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: Did you offer to me slaughtered victims and sacrifices in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel, and you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rompha, the figures which you made to worship them?' And in Paul, educated exactly in the things of the Jews and later from an unexpected/marvellous appearance of Jesus having become Christian, such things have been said in the [letter] to the Colossians: 'Let no one rob you of the prize, wishing in humility and worship of the angels, entering into the things he has seen, vainly puffed up by the mind of his flesh, and not holding the head, from which the whole body, supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows the growth of God.' These things Celsus having neither read nor learned, I know not how, has made [it] as though Jews not transgressing the law worship heaven and the angels in it.

pass_b_english: Since we say that he was confused by certain things he misheard, come, let us for our part make these points clear too, as far as we can, and show that, though Celsus thinks it a Jewish practice to worship heaven and the angels in it, such a practice is not Jewish but a transgression of Judaism, as is the worship of the sun, the moon and the stars, and of images too. You will find, at any rate, especially in Jeremiah, the word of God reproaching the Jewish people through the prophet for worshipping such things and for sacrificing “to the queen of heaven” (Jeremiah 44:17–19) and “to all the host of heaven” (Jeremiah 19:13).

The writings of the Christians also show, when they denounce the sins committed among the Jews, that once God had abandoned that people for certain sins, they committed these sins as well. For in the Acts of the Apostles it is written about the Jews: “But God turned and gave them over to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: Did you offer me slain beasts and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel? And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rompha, the figures which you made in order to worship them” (Acts 7:42–43; Amos 5:25–26).

And in Paul, who was strictly trained in the ways of the Jews (Acts 22:3) and later became a Christian through an extraordinary appearance of Jesus (Acts 9:3–6), such things are said in the letter to the Colossians: “Let no one disqualify you, insisting on humility and the worship of angels, dwelling on what he has seen, puffed up without cause by the mind of his flesh, and not holding fast to the Head, from whom the whole body, supplied and knit together through its joints and ligaments, grows with the growth that is from God” (Colossians 2:18–19).
But Celsus, having neither read nor learned these things, has represented the Jews, I do not know how, as worshipping heaven and the angels in it without breaking the law.
notes: Jeremiah: 'the queen of heaven' (τῇ βασιλίσσῃ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ) is LXX Jeremiah 51:17-19, which is English Jeremiah 44:17-19 (also 44:25; at Jeremiah 7:18 the LXX reads 'the host of heaven' instead of 'the queen of heaven'). 'To all the host of heaven' (πάσῃ τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ) matches Jeremiah 19:13 (cf. 8:2); chapter numbering in Jeremiah 19 is the same in LXX and English. Acts 7:42-43 quotes Amos 5:25-26 LXX; Origen's text reads the god's name as Ῥομφᾶ (NA: Ῥαιφάν, 'Rephan'), kept as 'Rompha'. Koetschau punctuates the whole quotation as one question; the question mark is placed after 'O house of Israel' as in the biblical text, without change of sense. 'Strictly trained in the ways of the Jews' is a clear echo of Acts 22:3 (πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν); 'an extraordinary appearance of Jesus' (ἐκ παραδόξου ἐπιφανείας) refers to the Damascus road (Acts 9:3-6). Colossians 2:18 θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ is the Septuagintal idiom 'delighting in / insisting on'; ἃ ἑώρακεν ἐμβατεύων rendered 'dwelling on what he has seen'. τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ θεοῦ rendered 'the growth that is from God'. ἀγάλμασιν rendered 'images'. φέρε kept as 'come'; ἡμεῖς and καὶ ταῦτα as 'for our part' and 'these points too'.
Pass A: the inline Greek lemma tags were moved out of the gloss into lemmas[] (the gloss was over a quarter Greek); the English gloss is unchanged.
